elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's affiliates.
elements.evidence: Rendered s.2 grants "to Customer, and to any affiliate of Customer identified in written notice to Kubient"; "Customer" is defined as The Associated Press alone, so the affiliate extension is new and non-duplicative.

elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: The rendered grant names only Customer and notified affiliates; no reference to contractors, agents or other parties acting on Customer's behalf. To meet this, the grant must add "and contractors acting on Customer's behalf".
The grant is a royalty-free access licence tied to the Services with no perpetuity language; the retained term/termination structure (s.4) leaves the licence coterminous with the Agreement.

The rendered clause still reads "without right of sublicense, revocable license" — the word "revocable" was retained, so no irrevocability. Note the deterministic check "no at-will revocation remains" is contradicted on the face of the text.

elements.element: A subscription licence is terminable only for uncured material breach.
elements.evidence: No limitation on revocation/termination grounds was inserted; the licence remains "revocable" and s.4's mutual post-Initial-Term termination and revocation-on-termination mechanics are untouched (as the drafter concedes).

elements.element: The licence is transferable to Customer's successors.
elements.evidence: Rendered s.2 now reads "transferable to a successor of Customer by merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all of its assets", and the conflicting "non-transferable, non-assignable" words were deleted.

elements.element: Customer's affiliates are covered on written notice.
elements.evidence: "Kubient hereby grants to Customer, and to any affiliate of Customer identified in written notice to Kubient" — the coverage mechanic is exactly notice-based, and the defined "Customer" (The Associated Press) does not already include affiliates.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction.
elements.evidence: "transferable to a successor of Customer by merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all of its assets"; the prior "non-transferable, non-assignable" bar was removed so no retained sentence contradicts it, and the transfer right runs one way (to Customer's successor) without creating any new Vendor assignment exception.

reasons: Fallback is position-complete: both fallback elements are met in operative language — affiliate coverage on written notice and successor transferability by merger, acquisition or asset sale — so the redline achieves an acceptable level.

Preferred is not complete: contractors acting on Customer's behalf are still excluded, "revocable" is retained, and there is no perpetual/irrevocable or breach-only-revocation language. To reach preferred the drafter would need to (i) add "and contractors acting on its behalf" to the grantee list, (ii) delete "revocable", and (iii) limit revocation to uncured material breach with conforming edits to s.4(a)/(c)(ii).

The deterministic check "no at-will revocation remains" is not borne out in substance — the rendered grant still says "revocable license". This does not defeat the fallback (revocability is not a fallback element) and the clause is no longer in walk-away territory because affiliates now have a path in, but the check should not be relied on as evidence of irrevocability.

Minimality holds: the only deletions are "non-transferable, non-assignable", which would directly contradict the new successor-transfer right, and the only insertions are the two fallback mechanics. Favourable existing language (royalty-free, non-exclusive, no sublicense, purpose scope, second sentence) is retained and no extra obligations, procedures or survival tails were added.

Intent preserved: s.2's commercial scope (ad serving/Auction Platform, Target Demand purpose) is unchanged; the assignment clause (h) is untouched and remains consistent, since it already permits assignment to a successor by merger/stock sale/consolidation and no new Vendor-side exception was created. No undefined terms or dangling cross-references result.

Residual note for the drafter (not a failure): deleting "non-transferable, non-assignable" outright leaves the grant silent on transfers generally rather than expressly limited to successors; if Kubient objects, offer "non-transferable except to a successor of Customer by merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all of its assets" as the same-effect narrower formulation.
